paraphrase: On 'then, therefore, the inquiry into Brahman', Bhāskara takes 'then' to mean after the inquiry into ritual duty: the two Mīmāṃsās form one continuous teaching, and knowledge of Brahman presupposes and is joined with the knowledge and performance of works.
notes: Content recalled at the level of Bhāskara's known position; exact wording at 1.1.1 to verify.

paraphrase: Bhāskara denounces those who, expounding the doctrine of māyā — disputed, cut off from its root and 'sung by the Mahāyāna Buddhists' — lead people astray.
notes: The phrase māhāyānika-bauddha-gāthitaṃ māyāvādam is well attested for Bhāskara; its location (commonly cited ad BS 1.4.25) must be verified.

paraphrase: On 'because of transformation of itself' (ātmakṛteḥ pariṇāmāt): Brahman makes itself into the world; the world is a real transformation of Brahman through its power, so Brahman is both the material and the efficient cause.

On the non-difference of effect from cause (tadananyatvam): the effect is real and is both different and non-different from its cause, as pots from clay; Bhāskara rejects the reading that the modification is 'a mere name' in the sense of being unreal.

On the soul as a part (aṃśa) of Brahman: the soul is a part of Brahman, different from it by its limiting adjuncts (upādhi) — the intellect and the rest, which are real — and non-different from it by nature (aupādhika-bhedābheda).

Bhāskara holds that liberation is not attained while the body lasts: the embodied knower still bears real adjuncts; knowledge combined with prescribed works continues until death, after which the soul, freed of adjuncts, becomes non-different from Brahman.
notes: Pāda-level reference (BS 4.1, esp. 4.1.13–19); exact sūtra to verify.

paraphrase: Bhartṛprapañca (as reported by Śaṅkara, identified by Ānandagiri) held that Brahman is both dual and non-dual, one and many, like the ocean and its waves: the manifold world is a real modification of the one Brahman.
notes: Reported by opponents: Śaṅkara's Bṛhadāraṇyaka commentary (on 5.1.1) with Ānandagiri's identification. Locus to verify.

paraphrase: Bhartṛprapañca (as reported and refuted by Śaṅkara and Sureśvara) taught that liberation requires the combination of knowledge with the Vedic works prescribed for one's station, throughout life.
notes: Reported by opponents (Śaṅkara's Bṛhadāraṇyaka commentary; Sureśvara's Vārttika). Exact loci to verify.

paraphrase: The soul is of the nature of knowledge, dependent on Hari, fit to be joined with and separated from bodies, atomic, different in each body, a knower, and infinite in number.
Souls are bound, their form covered by beginningless māyā, or released by the Lord's grace; the released are of different kinds.
The non-conscious (acit) is of three kinds: the non-material (aprākṛta), the material (prākṛta) and time (kāla).
Let us meditate on Kṛṣṇa, the lotus-eyed Hari, the supreme Brahman, who by nature is free of every fault, is the single mass of all auspicious qualities and has the vyūhas as his limbs.

original.text: svabhāvato 'pāsta-samasta-doṣam aśeṣa-kalyāṇa-guṇaika-rāśim | vyūhāṅginaṃ brahma paraṃ vareṇyaṃ dhyāyema kṛṣṇaṃ kamalekṣaṇaṃ harim ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

notes: Verse number (4) moderate confidence; some editions may number differently.

paraphrase: Let us remember the goddess, daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, shining joyfully on his left side, of matching beauty, always served by thousands of sakhīs, granting all desired ends.
notes: Among the earliest doctrinal texts to name Rādhā as the Lord's consort in worship.

paraphrase: This (Brahman) is always to be worshipped by people for the removal of the darkness of ignorance; so it was taught by Sanandana and the other sages to Nārada, the witness of all truths.
All knowledge is true, since according to scripture everything has Brahman as its self; the threefold nature (cit, acit, Īśvara) is established by scripture and the sūtras.
No other refuge is seen than Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, worshipped by Brahmā, Śiva and the rest, who takes a form at his devotees' wish, whose power is inconceivable and whose intent is beyond thought.

His grace arises for one endowed with humility and the like; by it arises devotion marked by special love for the Lord who has no other master; that devotion is the highest (parā), and there is also the devotion that is a means (sādhana).
The five things to be known by the wise: the nature of the one to be worshipped, of the worshipper, the fruit of grace, the rasa of devotion, and the nature of the obstacles to attaining him.
Brahman transforms itself into the world by its own power while remaining itself; the world is its real effect.
The soul is a part (aṃśa) of Brahman, since scripture declares both difference and non-difference between them; being a part it is both different and non-different from the whole.
Because scripture teaches both, the relation of the non-conscious world to Brahman is like that of the snake to its coils: difference and non-difference both hold.
notes: BS 3.2.27 (ahikuṇḍalavat) is the school's key sūtra; the next sūtras (light and its source) are also read as bhedābheda.

paraphrase: The released soul exists in non-separation (avibhāga) from Brahman, as seen in scripture, while remaining a distinct knower who enjoys Brahman's nature.
On 'that from which the birth etc. of this (world) proceed': that cause is Parameśvara Śiva, who with his cit-śakti is both the material and the efficient cause of the world.
The small space (dahara) within the lotus of the heart (Chāndogya 8.1) is Brahman — Śiva as the supreme ether (paramākāśa), which is his cit-śakti — and is the object of the dahara meditation.

Śrīkaṇṭha declares that he sees no difference between the Veda and the Śivāgama: both are authoritative as coming from Śiva; what the sūtras reject is only a view of the Lord as merely the efficient cause.
notes: Adhikaraṇa BS 2.2.37–41 (patyuḥ); sūtra-level locus of the statement to verify.

paraphrase: The released soul attains all the Lord's powers except the activity of the world (creation, maintenance, dissolution): it becomes equal to Śiva in bliss and knowledge, not identical with him.
The means of valid knowledge are four: the Vedas, the words of Śrī Kṛṣṇa (the Gītā), the sūtras of Vyāsa, and Vyāsa's 'language of trance' (the Bhāgavata).

original.text: vedāḥ śrīkṛṣṇavākyāni vyāsasūtrāṇi caiva hi | samādhibhāṣā vyāsasya pramāṇaṃ tac catuṣṭayam ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

notes: Wording recalled; the verse is widely quoted. Vallabha adds that each later source removes doubts about the earlier.

paraphrase: In the first part (Śāstrārtha-prakaraṇa) Vallabha teaches that the world is Brahman's own real form produced without change in Brahman, that only saṃsāra — the soul's ignorance-made 'I and mine' — is to be destroyed, and that souls are parts of Brahman whose bliss is concealed.
notes: Prakaraṇa-level reference; verse numbers to supply in Phase D.

paraphrase: Brahman, by transforming itself, is the material cause of the world; this transformation involves no change in Brahman (avikṛta-pariṇāma), as gold remains gold in its ornaments.
notes: The gold simile is standard in Śuddhādvaita exposition; its presence at this sūtra to verify.

paraphrase: Brahman is the locus of contradictory attributes (viruddha-dharmāśraya): scripture's statements that it is with and without qualities, near and far, moving and unmoving are all true of it, and are not to be divided into higher and lower truths.
notes: Pāda-level reference; the doctrine is central to Vallabha, the exact locus to verify.

paraphrase: What was spoken directly by the Lord at midnight on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight of Śrāvaṇa is now told word for word.

original.text: śrāvaṇasyāmale pakṣe ekādaśyāṃ mahāniśi | sākṣād bhagavatā proktaṃ tad akṣaraśa ucyate ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Vallabha

paraphrase: By making the relation with Brahman (brahmasambandha), all faults of body and soul are removed. The faults are of five kinds: innate, arising from place and time, those determined by worldly and Vedic rule, those from association and those from contact; none of them should be thought to remain.

Therefore what has not been offered is to be avoided; those who have dedicated themselves should do everything only after offering it, as a gift already given is not given again; like the Gaṅgā purifying what enters it, offering to the Lord removes faults.
notes: Verse range approximate.

paraphrase: Service (sevā) is the mind flowing toward him; to accomplish it there is service with body and with wealth; from that comes cessation of the sorrow of saṃsāra and the knowledge of Brahman.

original.text: cetas tat-pravaṇaṃ sevā tat-siddhyai tanu-vittajā | tataḥ saṃsāra-duḥkhasya nivṛttir brahma-bodhanam ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: The one reality appears in three ways, like the Gaṅgā: to the worldly as mere water, to the ritualist as a sacred river conferring merit, to the devotee as a goddess; so Brahman is seen as the world, as Akṣara Brahman and as Puruṣottama.
notes: Verse range approximate.

paraphrase: At all times and with one's whole being the Lord of Vraja is to be worshipped; this alone is one's dharma, and no other anywhere, ever.

original.text: sarvadā sarvabhāvena bhajanīyo vrajādhipaḥ | svasyāyam eva dharmo hi nānyaḥ kvāpi kadācana ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: When all paths are destroyed in the Kali age of wicked conduct and the world is full of heresy, Kṛṣṇa alone is my refuge.
notes: Each verse ends with the refrain kṛṣṇa eva gatir mama.

paraphrase: Discrimination (viveka), fortitude (dhairya) and refuge (āśraya) in the Lord are always to be guarded: discrimination that the Lord does all by his will, fortitude in bearing suffering, refuge in him alone.
Those who have offered themselves to the Lord should never have any anxiety, for the Lord, who does all by his own will, will not treat his own as worldly.

When the seed of devotion (given by grace) is made firm through renunciation, hearing and singing, it grows: love (sneha/prema) destroys attachment to other things, attachment (āsakti) makes the home distasteful, and when there is consuming absorption (vyasana) in Kṛṣṇa one has attained the goal.
notes: Verse numbers approximate.

paraphrase: Service bears three fruits — a supernatural capacity (to enjoy the Lord's bliss), union (sāyujya), and a body fit for service in the Lord's abode — and meets three obstacles: agitation (udvega), hindrance (pratibandha) and enjoyment (bhoga).

There are three creations of souls: those of grace (puṣṭi), chosen by the Lord for loving service; those of rule (maryādā), who follow scriptural discipline toward liberation; and those of the stream (pravāha), who pursue worldly ends (associated with the 'demonic' creation of Gītā 16); puṣṭi souls are further subdivided.
notes: Text-level reference; verse loci to supply.

paraphrase: Nirodha is the soul's absorption in the Lord through forgetting the world, brought about by the Lord's play; its highest form is the gopīs' longing in separation, and those absorbed in him are freed from saṃsāra.

In the path of devotion renunciation is not the knowledge-path renunciation of the world as false; it is appropriate only when love in separation (viraha) makes household life impossible, and taken otherwise in the Kali age it can become an obstacle.
notes: Summary-level; verse loci to supply.

paraphrase: His lips are sweet, his face is sweet, his eyes are sweet, his smile is sweet, his heart is sweet, his gait is sweet — everything of the lord of sweetness is sweet.

original.text: adharaṃ madhuraṃ vadanaṃ madhuraṃ nayanaṃ madhuraṃ hasitaṃ madhuram | hṛdayaṃ madhuraṃ gamanaṃ madhuraṃ madhurādhipater akhilaṃ madhuram ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: Among the Purāṇa's ten topics, maintenance (sthiti) is the victory of Vaikuṇṭha, and nourishment (poṣaṇa) is his grace (anugraha).
notes: The Puṣṭimārga takes 'poṣaṇa = anugraha' as the scriptural root of 'puṣṭi'. Primary owner of BhP teachings: U07.

paraphrase: Ignorance (avidyā) has five joints — forgetting one's own nature and the false identification with body, senses, vital breath and inner organ — and knowledge (vidyā) has five parts, among which devotion to Kṛṣṇa is chief.
notes: Recalled with low confidence; locate in the Śāstrārtha-prakaraṇa.

paraphrase: Victory to the congregational chanting of Kṛṣṇa's names, which cleanses the mirror of the mind, extinguishes the forest fire of worldly existence, spreads the moonlight of welfare, is the life of the bride of knowledge, increases the ocean of bliss, gives a taste of full nectar at every step and bathes the whole self.

original.text: ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanaṃ bhava-mahā-dāvāgni-nirvāpaṇaṃ śreyaḥ-kairava-candrikā-vitaraṇaṃ vidyā-vadhū-jīvanam | ānandāmbudhi-vardhanaṃ prati-padaṃ pūrṇāmṛtāsvādanaṃ sarvātma-snapanaṃ paraṃ vijayate śrī-kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtanam ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: You have made many names and placed all your powers in them, with no fixed rule of time for remembering them; such is your mercy, O Lord, yet such is my misfortune that I have no attraction for them.

original.text: nāmnām akāri bahudhā nija-sarva-śaktis tatrārpitā niyamitaḥ smaraṇe na kālaḥ | etādṛśī tava kṛpā bhagavan mamāpi durdaivam īdṛśam ihājani nānurāgaḥ ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: Humbler than a blade of grass, more tolerant than a tree, giving respect to others and not expecting it for oneself — so should one always sing (the names of) Hari.

original.text: tṛṇād api sunīcena taror api sahiṣṇunā | amāninā mānadena kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: I desire neither wealth, nor followers, nor beautiful women, nor poetry, O Lord of the world; may there be causeless devotion to you, my Lord, birth after birth.

original.text: na dhanaṃ na janaṃ na sundarīṃ kavitāṃ vā jagad-īśa kāmaye | mama janmani janmanīśvare bhavatād bhaktir ahaitukī tvayi ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: O son of Nanda, consider me, your servant fallen into the terrible ocean of existence, by your mercy as a particle of dust at your lotus feet.
speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: When will my eyes stream with tears, my voice falter and choke, and my body bristle with horripilation as I take your name?
speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: In separation from Govinda a moment seems an age, my eyes pour like the rains, and the whole world seems empty.

original.text: yugāyitaṃ nimeṣeṇa cakṣuṣā prāvṛṣāyitam | śūnyāyitaṃ jagat sarvaṃ govinda-viraheṇa me ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: Let him embrace me, devoted to his feet, or trample me, or break my heart by not appearing; let that libertine do as he likes — he alone, and no other, is the lord of my life.

original.text: āśliṣya vā pāda-ratāṃ pinaṣṭu mām adarśanān marma-hatāṃ karotu vā | yathā tathā vā vidadhātu lampaṭo mat-prāṇa-nāthas tu sa eva nāparaḥ ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya (in the mood of Rādhā)

paraphrase: The highest devotion (uttamā bhakti) is the cultivation of (activity for) Kṛṣṇa in a favourable spirit, free of desire for anything else and not covered by knowledge (aiming at impersonal oneness), ritual works and the like.

original.text: anyābhilāṣitā-śūnyaṃ jñāna-karmādy-anāvṛtam | ānukūlyena kṛṣṇānuśīlanaṃ bhaktir uttamā ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: Pure devotion destroys suffering, bestows auspiciousness, makes liberation seem trivial, is very rarely attained, is of the nature of intense bliss, and attracts Kṛṣṇa.

original.text: kleśa-ghnī śubhadā mokṣa-laghutā-kṛt sudurlabhā | sāndrānanda-viśeṣātmā śrī-kṛṣṇākarṣiṇī ca sā ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

notes: Verse number moderately certain.

paraphrase: (Quoting the Padma Purāṇa:) for those devoted to Viṣṇu, sin not yet bearing fruit, sin in its latent stage, its seed, and sin about to bear fruit are destroyed in sequence.
notes: Verse number to verify.

paraphrase: Devotion is said to be threefold: practice (sādhana), emotion (bhāva) and love (prema). Practice is devotion accomplished by the senses and aiming at bhāva; its attainment is only the manifestation in the heart of an eternally perfect emotion.
Where, rāga not having been attained, activity arises only through the command of scripture, that is called devotion by rule (vaidhī bhakti).
(Quoting the Padma Purāṇa:) Viṣṇu is always to be remembered and never forgotten; all injunctions and prohibitions are servants of these two.
notes: Verse number to verify.

paraphrase: As long as the witch of desire for enjoyment and liberation remains in the heart, how can the joy of devotion arise there?

original.text: bhukti-mukti-spṛhā yāvat piśācī hṛdi vartate | tāvad bhakti-sukhasyātra katham abhyudayo bhavet ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

notes: Verse number moderately certain.

paraphrase: Rūpa enumerates sixty-four limbs of practice (from taking shelter of a guru's feet, receiving initiation and instruction and serving the guru with trust, through the ten avoidances, to hearing, chanting, remembering and deity service) and names five as most potent: serving the deity with faith, relishing the Bhāgavata with the like-minded, association with advanced devotees, congregational chanting of the name and residence in Mathurā.
notes: Laharī-level reference (the list runs through much of BRS 1.2); verse numbers to supply.

paraphrase: One whose every effort — by action, mind and speech — is for the service of Hari, in all circumstances, is called liberated while living (jīvanmukta).
notes: Verse number to verify.

paraphrase: (Quoting the Padma Purāṇa:) the name is a wish-fulfilling gem, Kṛṣṇa himself, the embodiment of consciousness and rasa, complete, pure, eternally free, because the name and the named are non-different. Therefore Kṛṣṇa's name and the rest cannot be grasped by the senses; it manifests of itself on a tongue and senses turned toward service.
notes: Verse numbers moderately certain.

paraphrase: Detachment is fitting (yukta-vairāgya) when one uses things as appropriate without attachment, with insistence on their relation to Kṛṣṇa; renunciation of things related to Hari by those seeking liberation, considering them worldly, is called futile detachment (phalgu-vairāgya).

Rāgātmikā devotion is that full of rāga — spontaneous, intense absorption in the beloved — as found in the residents of Vraja; devotion that follows it is rāgānugā, of two kinds: following desire (kāmānugā) and following relationship (sambandhānugā).
notes: Verse range approximate.

paraphrase: The sign that eager longing (lobha) has arisen is that, on hearing of the sweetness of the Vraja residents' emotions, the mind does not look to scripture or reasoning (for its motive).
notes: Verse number to verify.

paraphrase: Remembering Kṛṣṇa and his beloved associate suited to one's own longing, absorbed in their stories, one should always live in Vraja; service is to be done both in the practitioner's form and in the perfected form, by one desiring that emotion, following the people of Vraja.

original.text: sevā sādhaka-rūpeṇa siddha-rūpeṇa cātra hi | tad-bhāva-lipsunā kāryā vraja-lokānusārataḥ ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

notes: The quoted original is verse 295.

paraphrase: Bhāva is of the nature of special pure sattva, is like a ray of the sun of prema, and softens the heart with tastes (for the Lord).

original.text: śuddha-sattva-viśeṣātmā prema-sūryāṃśu-sāmya-bhāk | rucibhiś citta-māsṛṇya-kṛd asau bhāva ucyate ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: In one in whom bhāva has sprouted appear: forbearance, not wasting time, detachment, freedom from pride, hope, eager longing, constant taste for singing the name, attachment to describing his qualities, and affection for his dwelling places.
notes: Verse numbers moderately certain.

paraphrase: Rūpa distinguishes true bhāva from its semblances (ratyābhāsa), reflected and shadow-like, which appear in those whose hearts are not pure or whose aims are other than devotion; outward signs alone do not prove bhāva.
notes: Laharī-level reference.

paraphrase: When bhāva becomes dense, thoroughly softening the heart and marked by an excess of the sense of possessiveness (mamatā) toward the Lord, the wise call it prema.

original.text: samyaṅ-masṛṇita-svānto mamatvātiśayāṅkitaḥ | bhāvaḥ sa eva sāndrātmā budhaiḥ premā nigadyate ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: First faith, then association with saints, then devotional practice, then the removal of unwanted things, then steadiness, then taste, then attachment, then emotion (bhāva), then love (prema) arises: this is the sequence of the appearance of love for practitioners.

original.text: ādau śraddhā tataḥ sādhu-saṅgo 'tha bhajana-kriyā | tato 'nartha-nivṛttiḥ syāt tato niṣṭhā rucis tataḥ || athāsaktis tato bhāvas tataḥ premābhyudañcati | sādhakānām ayaṃ premṇaḥ prādurbhāve bhavet kramaḥ ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: Rūpa sets out the components of bhakti-rasa: the permanent emotion (sthāyibhāva, love for Kṛṣṇa) becomes rasa when combined with its excitants (vibhāva: the object, Kṛṣṇa and his devotees, and the stimuli), its outward effects (anubhāva), the involuntary bodily signs (sāttvika) and the transient emotions (vyabhicārin); Kṛṣṇa's sixty-four qualities are described, four unique to him.
notes: Vibhāga-level reference (southern division, BRS 2.1–2.5).

paraphrase: The eight sāttvika signs — stupor, sweating, horripilation, breaking of the voice, trembling, change of colour, tears and loss of consciousness — appear with degrees of intensity (smouldering, flaming, burning, blazing).
Thirty-three transient emotions (vyabhicārī-bhāva), from despondency (nirveda) to awakening (bodha), rise and fall like waves in the ocean of the permanent emotion.

The five primary devotional rasas are: peaceful (śānta), servitude (prīta/dāsya), friendship (preyas/sakhya), parental affection (vatsala) and amorous love (madhura); each rests on its own permanent emotion toward Kṛṣṇa, and they rise in intensity of relish.
notes: Vibhāga-level reference (western division).

paraphrase: The seven secondary rasas — humour, wonder, heroism, compassion, anger, fear and disgust — arise within devotion occasionally; mixing incompatible rasas produces only a semblance of rasa (rasābhāsa).
notes: Vibhāga-level reference (northern division).

paraphrase: The poets do not approve of another's wife as heroine in the principal rasa — except for the lotus-eyed women of Gokula, since Kṛṣṇa, crown of connoisseurs, brought them down (into the world) to taste rasa.
notes: Commonly cited as UN 1.21 (nāyaka-bheda); number and wording to verify.

paraphrase: Love (prema) intensifies through stages — affection (sneha), love-pique (māna), intimacy (praṇaya), passion (rāga), ever-new passion (anurāga) and great emotion (mahābhāva) — the last found only in the gopīs of Vraja and, in its highest forms, in Rādhā alone.
notes: Chapter-level reference (the chapter on the permanent emotion).

paraphrase: Rādhā is the greatest of the gopīs, the embodiment of mahābhāva and Kṛṣṇa's hlādinī-śakti, endowed with innumerable qualities; the sakhīs and mañjarīs serve her.
notes: Chapter-level reference.

paraphrase: A steady person who can tolerate the urges of speech, of the mind, of anger, of the tongue, of the belly and of the genitals can make disciples of the whole world.

original.text: vāco vegaṃ manasaḥ krodha-vegaṃ jihvā-vegam udaropastha-vegam | etān vegān yo viṣaheta dhīraḥ sarvām apīmāṃ pṛthivīṃ sa śiṣyāt ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: Devotion is destroyed by six things: overeating (or over-collecting), over-endeavour, idle talk, rigid attachment to rules (or neglect of them), worldly company and greed/fickleness.

original.text: atyāhāraḥ prayāsaś ca prajalpo niyamāgrahaḥ | jana-saṅgaś ca laulyaṃ ca ṣaḍbhir bhaktir vinaśyati ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: Devotion succeeds through six things: enthusiasm, conviction, patience, performing the prescribed activities, giving up bad company and following the conduct of the saints.

original.text: utsāhān niścayād dhairyāt tat-tat-karma-pravartanāt | saṅga-tyāgāt sato vṛtteḥ ṣaḍbhir bhaktiḥ prasidhyati ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

paraphrase: Giving and receiving gifts, revealing and inquiring about confidential matters, eating and feeding — these six are the signs of love among devotees.

One who utters the name 'Kṛṣṇa' is to be honoured in the mind; one who has taken initiation and worships, with obeisances; one who is advanced in exclusive worship and free of fault-finding, with service and association.

The essence of all instruction: engaging the tongue and mind in turn in singing and remembering his name, form, qualities and play, one should pass all one's time living in Vraja, following those who are attached to him.

paraphrase: Above Vaikuṇṭha is Mathurā, above it Vṛndāvana, above it Govardhana, and above all Rādhākuṇḍa, the pond as dear to Kṛṣṇa as Rādhā herself; bathing there awakens the highest love.
